title: Case study: fall in long-term care
text:
Long-term care facility, night shift. An 84-year-old resident with Parkinson disease, atrial fibrillation, osteoporosis and mild dementia is found on the floor.

History: Parkinson disease for 8 years. Atrial fibrillation. Osteoporosis. Mild dementia. No known drug allergies. Weight 62 kg. Code status: full code. Baseline on the care plan: walks with a walker and standby assistance, oriented to person and place, and uses the call light inconsistently.

At 0240 the assistive personnel (AP) calls the PN. The resident is sitting on the floor beside the bed and says, "I needed the bathroom and didn't want to bother anyone."

Medications
- carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 mg PO three times daily
- apixaban 5 mg PO twice daily
- alendronate 70 mg PO weekly
- donepezil 5 mg PO at bedtime
- zolpidem 5 mg PO at bedtime, started 3 nights ago

| 0245 data collection | Finding |
|---|---|
| BP | 104/62 mm Hg sitting (afternoon reading 132/78) |
| Heart rate | 92/min, irregular |
| Respirations | 18/min |
| Temperature | 97.8 F |
| Pain | Right hip 2 of 10; no shortening or rotation of the leg |
| Head | Small bump above the left ear, skin intact; speech clear, no facial droop |
| Orientation | Person and place, same as baseline |
| Room | Bed in the low position, call light on the floor, floor dry, resident barefoot |

title: Case study: hypoglycemia in a long-term care resident
text:
Long-term care facility, 1130. A 79-year-old resident with type 2 diabetes for 20 years, hypertension and mild chronic kidney disease. Weight 61 kg. No known allergies.

Baseline, per the assistive personnel (AP) who care for her every day: alert, oriented to person and place, chats during care, and walks to the dining room with a walker. Usual blood pressure is in the 130s/80s. She eats in the dining room and takes her morning medicines there.

The AP reports that the resident ate about 25% of breakfast at 0800, saying her stomach was upset, and that the 0800 medicines were given. At 1130 the AP finds her in her room, says she "does not seem like herself," and calls the PN. A bedside glucose has not been checked yet.

Medications
- glipizide 10 mg PO before breakfast
- insulin glargine 20 units subcut at bedtime (last dose 2100 yesterday)
- lisinopril 20 mg PO daily
- atorvastatin 20 mg PO at bedtime

| 1130 data | Finding |
|---|---|
| BP | 138/82 mm Hg |
| Heart rate | 104/min |
| Respirations | 20/min |
| Temperature | 97.9 F |
| SpO2 | 96% on room air |
| Skin | Cool and sweaty |
| Breakfast | About 25% eaten; glipizide given at 0800 |

title: Case study: depression at a diabetes clinic visit
text:
Outpatient diabetes clinic, 1000. A 58-year-old client with type 2 diabetes, hypertension and obesity comes in for a 3-month follow-up. The client's spouse died 5 months ago. The client lives alone and has stopped attending the weekly diabetes support group.

Medications: metformin 1,000 mg PO twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg PO daily, atorvastatin 20 mg PO at bedtime. No known allergies. The chart does not yet record whether today's doses were taken.

The client says, "I don't see the point in checking my sugar anymore."

| Clinic data | Today | 3 months ago |
|---|---|---|
| Weight | 88 kg | 95 kg |
| BP | 148/88 mm Hg | 134/82 mm Hg |
| A1C | 9.4% | 7.6% |
| Glucose log | 6 entries in 3 months | 2 entries daily |
| Sleep | "4 hours, up at 3 a.m. most nights" | 7 hours |
| PHQ-2 score | 5 of 6 | 1 of 6 |
| Support | Lives alone; left the diabetes group after the death | Attended the group weekly |
